abstract: Rare alleles arise from mutations on an existing haplotype background, yet current gene-based rare variant association tests treat low-frequency coding variants as effects independent of the common regulatory variants that surround them. The penetrance of rare coding variants can be modulated by the cis-regulatory landscape, and failing to account for this context limits the statistical power of existing methods for complex traits. We present PrediXSKAT, a kernel-based rare variant association framework that incorporates the surrounding cis-regulatory landscape by estimating its impact on gene expression via PrediXcan. PrediXSKAT embeds predicted gene expression directly into the Sequence Kernel Association Test kernel through element-wise similarity weighting, concentrating rare variant signal among individuals who share concordant genetic and regulatory backgrounds. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that PrediXSKAT increases power over standard kernel-based testing under biologically realistic conditions where a proportion of tested variants carry small, mixed-direction effects. Type I error rates are controlled in the absence of association. Power gains persist across a range of sample sizes and causal variant architectures. Applied to whole-genome sequencing data from the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project, PrediXSKAT recapitulates established disease loci and amplifies signals at previously unreported candidate genes without indiscriminately inflating genome-wide results. PrediXSKAT provides a generalizable and extensible framework for the joint analysis of common regulatory and rare coding variants. The approach can be applied to any kernel-based set test and extended to jointly consider multiple genes within the same biological pathway, offering a principled strategy for improving rare variant discovery in large-scale sequencing studies of complex disease.
